title: Half of Australians Feel Overqualified for Their Jobs
paragraphs: Many people study hard to get a good job. But in Australia, almost half of workers believe they have more education than their job actually needs, according to new data.

The data comes from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey. This long-term study has followed about 17,000 people every year since 2001. Dr Inga Lass of the University of Melbourne, who is part of the team behind the survey, wrote about the findings in September.

In 2024, 49.5% of workers aged 18 to 64 were "overeducated." This means they had a higher level of education than they thought was needed to do their job well. In addition, 25.7% of workers were "overskilled," meaning they could not use many of their skills at work.
One reason may be that more Australians are going to university. The share of people aged 18 to 64 with a bachelor's degree rose from about 14% in 2001 to almost 22% in 2024.

Being overqualified seems to have a real cost for workers. Workers who were overeducated or overskilled were less satisfied with their jobs, including their pay and the work itself. They were also less satisfied with their lives in general, and they were more likely to think about quitting.

The problem often lasts a long time. Four years later, 65% of overeducated workers were still in the same situation. Some had stopped working altogether. Around 11% of overeducated workers were no longer employed after four years, compared with about 8% of workers whose jobs matched their education.

Some groups are more affected than others. Young people and casual workers were the most likely to be overqualified. The problem was also common in retail jobs, among laborers and drivers, and in hotels and restaurants.
